svg.title: Lab 02 — Routing between two /26 subnets
svg.desc: One /24 carved into two /26 networks; Router0 is the only way between them
svg.text: One /24 carved into two /26 networks; Router0 is the only way between them
THE /24 ADDRESS SPACE, SLICED INTO FOUR /26 BLOCKS (256 ADDRESSES)
PC1 .11/26 → .100 is outside .0–.63, so use the default gateway
PC1 broadcasts “who has 192.168.1.1?”; Router0 G0/0 replies
dst .100 matches connected network 192.168.1.64/26 → out G0/1
Router0 ARPs for .100, rewrites the Ethernet header, forwards
Orange rule: MAC addresses change at every hop; the IP pair stays the same.
Change a host to the wrong mask or gateway and watch exactly which step of the packet walk breaks.
Directly connected networks appear in the routing table automatically once the interface is up with an IP.
